artifact.title: Exact partial-involution dynamics faces a centrality-versus-Goldstone trilemma
artifact.status: exact orbit-dimension count and structural classification
artifact.question: Does imposing Q^3=Q dynamically remove radial collapse without introducing a large new angular sector?

spectrum.oneSided: On every robust 184-dimensional carrier, Tr Q=0 and Tr Q^2=88.
spectrum.fixedSpectrum: The polynomial Q^3=Q fixes eigenvalues but not eigenspaces if Q is allowed to range over all Hermitian matrices.

fullMatrixOrbit.sideDoubledUnrestricted: For diag(Q_L,Q_R) with multiplicities (88,88,192), unrestricted U(368) conjugation gives orbit dimension 83072.
fullMatrixOrbit.sideDoubledBlockPreserving: If the auxiliary side label forbids mixing, two independent one-sided orbits still give 41536 directions.
fullMatrixOrbit.implication: A bare polynomial constraint removes radial modes but leaves an enormous angular orbit unless most directions are gauge, explicitly lifted, or never admitted.

centralRestriction.statement: The repair construction requires Q to remain a central node-charge operator so that its commutator has the audited A/B selectivity.
centralRestriction.consequence: Within the fixed represented center and fixed support assignment, Q^3=Q leaves discrete eigenvalue choices rather than the full unitary conjugacy orbit.
centralRestriction.benefit: There are then no continuous angular Goldstones and no radial collapse.
centralRestriction.cost: Q behaves as discrete finite-geometric data or a superselection/order assignment, not as an ordinary adjoint Higgs field.

trilemma.problem: At least 20768 angular directions per one-sided carrier before gauging/lifting, and generic rotations destroy central selectivity.

trilemma.advantage: Exact repair selectivity, no radial mode, no angular orbit.
trilemma.problem: Its microscopic selection is discrete/kinematical and cannot be explained by the usual continuous Higgs mechanism alone.

trilemma.advantage: Some angular directions may be gauge-eaten.
trilemma.problem: A precise enlarged gauge group and stabilizer must be supplied; it must reduce to the finite algebra while preserving the desired carrier.

interpretation: The exact-constraint escape favored by v524-v527 is viable only if centrality is treated as part of the field definition, not merely as a vacuum property of a generic matrix.
Promoting Q to a generic adjoint creates far more structure than the original programme intended.
A discrete remnant or higher-form/topological order parameter is now a cleaner target than a conventional continuous scalar.
falsifiers: The admissible finite gauge group acts transitively on the full 20768-dimensional orbit and eats all unwanted directions without new light vectors.
The finite differential calculus kinematically removes noncentral tangent directions while still allowing a nontrivial dynamical central field.
Radiative corrections preserve a strictly central constraint without a protecting discrete or categorical symmetry.
The trace census changes after the exact KO6 representation, altering the multiplicities and orbit dimensions.
next: Construct a discrete Z2 or Z3 order parameter whose representation is Q and whose domain walls are classifiable.
Compute the actual gauge-orbit dimension of the represented finite algebra and compare it with 20768.
Test whether Q can be a central idempotent selected by algebra phase transition rather than a matrix scalar.
artifact.conclusion: The polynomial Q^3=Q solves radial collapse only cleanly when Q is restricted to the represented center. If Q is a generic matrix field, the same spectrum carries a 20768-dimensional angular orbit and loses the minimality of the repair.

artifact.title: A curvature-induced Q^2 term can rescue or destroy the soft compensator, depending on its signed coefficient
artifact.status: numerical-exact-piecewise phase map in the eleven-field truncation
artifact.question: Can the Cartan/spacetime piece of the product compensator supply the missing force that stabilizes a dynamical finite Q?

setup.benchmark: kappa=20/19, the radial/inactive maximin repair scale.
setup.potential: W=E_min(kappa y)+Lambda(y-1)^2+nu kappa^2 y, with y=q^2.
setup.normalization: m=Lambda/kappa^2; nu is the dimensionless signed Cartan/curvature coefficient.
setup.sign: Positive nu penalizes nonzero Q and strengthens collapse; negative nu favors nonzero Q.

exhaustive_result.method: The same 15 KKT-valid radial phases as v525 were minimized and compared for each (m,nu).

desiredNuBands.meaning: No desired global phase was found for -50<=nu<=50; the radial quartic is too weak and the minimum jumps between under- and over-repaired phases.

exhaustive_result.zeroCurvatureCheck: nu=0 first admits the desired global phase between m=4 and m=5, consistently with v525's critical m approximately 4.710198.

interpretation: The product construction contains a possible self-rescue: a sufficiently negative background Cartan contribution acts like a tachyonic q^2 term and can stabilize Q even when its standalone radial quartic is below the nu=0 threshold.
The rescue is a finite band, not an arbitrarily negative half-line. Too negative a coefficient overdrives delta beyond the desired phase window.
A positive Euclidean-looking Cartan norm does the opposite: it makes Q collapse more likely. Therefore the sign ambiguity exposed by the Krein audit is dynamically decisive, not cosmetic.
At m=2 the viable curvature band is already fairly narrow, while larger m broadens tolerance.
research_direction: Evaluate nu on an explicit AdS4/Spin(2,3) background instead of treating it as free.
Track analytic continuation: the Lorentzian signed Cartan term and Euclidean positive action need not induce the same nu.
Compute whether nu is proportional to scalar curvature, compensator kinetic energy, or both.
Check whether cosmological evolution crosses a band boundary and triggers a first-order finite-vacuum transition.
falsifiers: The correctly contracted product spectral action fixes nu outside the quoted viable band for the derived m.
The sign of the physical Cartan contribution is necessarily positive in every ghost-free continuation and m remains below the corresponding threshold.
Additional non-radial fields remove or substantially shift the finite band.
An analytic phase comparison disagrees with the enumerated boundaries.

reproducibility.scan: 4001-point nu bracketing on [-50,50] followed by 55 bisection steps at each boundary.

next: Derive nu from the explicit compensator covariant derivative on AdS4.
Replace constant nu by a curvature-dependent nu(R) and follow the phase along an FLRW history.
Compute exact algebraic expressions for the band edges.
artifact.conclusion: Spacetime geometry can in principle stabilize the same finite order parameter that repairs the vacuum, but only if the contracted Cartan term has the right signed magnitude. This turns the Krein/action prescription into a concrete phase-selection test.

artifact.title: Full KKT minimization reveals a first-order soft-Q transition beyond the local stiffness bound
artifact.status: exhaustive piecewise radial KKT census for the eleven-field truncation
artifact.correction_to_v524: The v524 stiffness inequality guarantees that the stationary point on the desired branch lies above the G-stability boundary. It does not by itself guarantee that this branch is the global minimum against all G-condensed phases.

method.variables: Eleven canonical squared orbit amplitudes plus y=q^2>=0, with delta=kappa y and unrestricted leakage ratio 1/4.
method.phaseEnumeration: All 2^11 active sets were tested; 15 have a nonempty KKT-valid delta interval.
method.elimination: For each phase, amplitudes are affine and minimized matter energy is quadratic in delta. Adding Lambda(delta/kappa-1)^2 gives an exactly minimized quadratic on each validity interval.
method.comparison: The minima of all 15 pieces were compared globally.

phase_boundaries.desired: The desired four-field phase is KKT-valid for 24/61 <= delta <= 24/11.
phase_boundaries.below: For delta<24/61 one or more competing phases contain G=(4,8).
phase_boundaries.collapse_endpoint: At delta=0 the best phase contains (1,7),(2,9),(4,8),(5,10).

global_transitions.character: Continuous contact with the desired phase at delta=24/61; below it the minimizing phase retains G.
First-order jump from a low-delta G phase near delta=0.09996 to the desired phase near delta=0.39660.
global_transitions.excess: approximately 2.92 percent above the local bound.

global_transitions.character: First-order jump from the collapsed delta=0 G phase to the desired phase near delta=0.75552.

benchmark_checks: At kappa=20/19 and Lambda/kappa^2=5, the global minimum is desired with delta approximately 0.77537 and y approximately 0.73660.
At kappa=20/19 and ratio 10, delta approximately 0.92384 and y approximately 0.87764.
At kappa=1/2 and ratio 20, delta approximately 0.41888 and y approximately 0.83775.
At kappa=2/5 and ratio 100, delta approximately 0.38171 and G remains active.
interpretation: The dynamical-Q problem has metastable branch competition, not merely a smooth radial displacement.
The maximin coupling remains much less stiff than the near-threshold coupling, but its true global requirement is materially stronger than the local Hessian estimate.
A first-order transition implies possible domain-wall, hysteresis, or cosmological trapping questions if Q is a genuine field.
Exact constraint Q^3=Q bypasses both radial collapse and this branch competition, at the cost of moving the burden to the constraint's microscopic origin.
falsifiers: Adding omitted orbit directions produces a lower non-G phase and removes the reported transition.
The full non-radial matrix potential invalidates reduction to squared canonical orbit amplitudes.
An exact rational comparison of phase energies yields different critical ratios beyond numerical tolerance.
Spin(2,3) Cartan or curvature contributions change the y potential enough to eliminate the competing collapsed phase.

reproducibility.tolerance: Double-precision enumeration and 70-step bisection; quoted thresholds are numerical.

next: Derive exact algebraic critical ratios for the two first-order transitions.
Compute the barrier height and thin-wall scale near the maximin transition.
Add a curvature-generated q^2 term and map the two-parameter phase diagram.
artifact.conclusion: The soft-Q completion is globally viable only above a phase-competition threshold. For the preferred maximin coupling the threshold is Lambda/kappa^2 about 4.7102, not merely the local 2.4869 bound.

artifact.title: A locked central Ising pair realizes Q without the adjoint Goldstone explosion
artifact.status: exact zero-dimensional potential and topological branch point
artifact.question: Can Q=P_A-P_B arise from a minimal discrete order parameter while preserving exact central selectivity?

construction.fields: Two real central amplitudes a and b with Q(a,b)=a P_A+b P_B; Q vanishes on the complementary central support.
construction.exactMinima: Because every summand is nonnegative, V=0 exactly at (a,b)=(1,-1) and (-1,1), hence Q=+/- (P_A-P_B).
construction.symmetry: The potential has a global Z2: (a,b)->(-a,-b).

local_stability.positivity: Trace and determinant are positive for positive couplings, so both central radial modes are massive.

selector.invariance: The repair norm is even under Q->-Q, so both vacua generate identical A-B masses and the same unrestricted/projected repair ray.
selector.centrality: No noncentral unitary conjugacy directions are admitted; the 20768-dimensional orbit of v528 is absent by field definition.
selector.product: C=N tensor Q also changes sign under either N or Q alone, while the minimal squared action is invariant.

topological_dichotomy.physicalZ2: If Q and -Q are distinct vacua of a global discrete symmetry, spatial interpolation supports domain walls once kinetic terms are supplied.
topological_dichotomy.gaugedDiagonal: If the theory identifies (N,Q)~(-N,-Q), the product C is unchanged and the two finite signs may be one physical configuration.
topological_dichotomy.obstruction: The antipodal N->-N map is not automatically in the connected Spin(2,3) gauge group; a Pin/O extension or explicit discrete gauge identification must be demonstrated.
topological_dichotomy.observationalHandle: Any term odd in Q, or coupling that distinguishes time orientation N from -N, makes the sign physical and restores the wall question.

relation_to_soft_backreaction: Finite lambda_A,lambda_B still permit amplitude shifts away from +/-1 when matter is included, so v524-v527 stiffness bounds reappear in a two-field form.
Taking the nonlinear-constraint limit removes radial backreaction exactly and leaves only the discrete sign.
The locking term kappa prevents independent A and B sign choices and makes the relative minus sign dynamical.
interpretation: A discrete central order parameter is substantially more economical than an unrestricted adjoint Higgs.
The research burden moves from stabilizing thousands of angular modes to deciding whether a single Z2 is global, gauged, or tied to spacetime orientation.
The simultaneous sign structure offers a concrete way the finite A/B grading could be linked to the Spin(2,3) compensator rather than merely appended to it.
falsifiers: The exact finite algebra does not admit P_A and P_B as separately represented central projectors.
Radiative corrections generate central terms that lift the relative-minus minima or require a third light amplitude.
No consistent discrete gauge extension identifies (N,Q) with (-N,-Q), while cosmological bounds exclude the resulting domain walls.
Odd-Q terms required elsewhere in the fermion or real-structure sector split the two minima incompatibly.
next: Audit the fermionic action and real structure for terms odd in Q.
Determine whether the antipodal compensator map lifts to an admissible Pin(2,3) or discrete gauge operation.
Add kinetic terms and estimate the domain-wall tension in the finite-lambda model.
Repeat the backreaction minimization with independent a and b.
artifact.conclusion: A locked pair of central Ising amplitudes gives exactly Q=+/-(P_A-P_B) with two massive radial modes and no adjoint angular sector. Its decisive question is whether the residual sign is a physical global Z2 with walls or a diagonal spacetime-finite gauge identification.

artifact.title: The minimal covariantly contracted product invariant ties positive repair to positive compensator mass
artifact.status: exact coefficient-ratio result under the explicit side-doubled product ansatz
artifact.question: Does the same minimal product invariant naturally generate the negative q^2 coefficient that can rescue a soft finite compensator?

assumptions.geometry: On the broken Spin(2,3)/Spin(1,3) background, D_a N=Gamma_a/ell for a=0,1,2,3.
assumptions.spinPairing: Use the v522 operator Krein-Hilbert-Schmidt form and contract residual indices with eta^{ab}.
assumptions.productTerm: Delta V=c <[D,C],[D,C]> with C=N tensor q Q_side and c positive so that the finite repair coefficient is positive.

exact_contractions.mixed: Every Cartan-finite mixed trace vanishes, as in v522.

reduction.finitePiece: Delta V_finite=c (4)||[D_F,q Q_side]||^2=16 c q^2 U(D_F).
reduction.relativeCoefficient: After factoring the finite repair coefficient 16c, the induced positive radial mass is 176 q^2/ell^2.
reduction.signLock: For c>0, both the finite repair and the covariantly contracted Cartan q^2 term are positive.

consequence.dynamicalQ: The minimal invariant supplies positive nu in the normalization of v526 and therefore strengthens, rather than cures, Q collapse.
consequence.fixedQ: If Q^3=Q is imposed exactly, the Cartan term is only a constant background normalization and does not move q.
consequence.requiredEscape: A soft-Q theory needs an additional negative curvature/nonminimal term, a shifted radial potential, or a trace/action prescription that breaks this sign lock while retaining a positive finite repair.

interpretation: The apparent Lorentz-indefiniteness of the component norm in v522 is necessary for covariance; after metric contraction it produces a positive scalar in four dimensions.
The rigid trace factor 176 from v523 makes the backreaction large rather than carrier-tunable.
The negative-nu rescue bands of v526 cannot be attributed to the same minimal positive product-square coefficient.
This favors the constrained-partial-involution interpretation over a freely soft radial Q in the minimal product model.
artifact.normalization_warning: The absolute number 176 depends on using the unnormalized finite trace. A normalized trace rescales both product pieces, but the relative factor remains the finite expectation of Q_side^2 in the chosen normalization; it cannot change the sign.
falsifiers: A complete Dirac/connection convention inserts an additional factor whose physically required continuation reverses only the Cartan q^2 term while preserving the finite repair sign.
Torsion or curvature cross terms survive the trace and provide a negative contribution larger than 176/ell^2.
The side-doubled KO6 construction changes Tr(Q_side^2) or the relation ||[D_F,Q_side]||^2=4U.
The physical action is not the covariantly contracted operator Krein-Hilbert-Schmidt square assumed here.
next: Test a nonminimal R q^2 invariant and determine the coefficient needed to overcome the +176/ell^2 mass.
Implement the side doublet with grading and real structure to audit the coefficient relation.
Explore whether a Lagrange-multiplier partial involution arises as a low-energy limit of a heavy adjoint Higgs.
artifact.conclusion: Under the minimal product-square prescription, the sign that makes the finite A-B repair positive also gives Q a positive Cartan mass. The same invariant therefore cannot dynamically self-stabilize a soft Q; exact constraint or additional signed structure is required.
